headline: Climate talks run into overtime, three leaders meet in China, and the AI boom hits a wobble.

items.title: Trump in Shenzhen for APEC and a first three-way meeting with Xi and Putin
items.summary: US President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen for the APEC summit and a planned meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. The agenda includes Russia's war in Ukraine, the US war with Iran, trade, AI and nuclear weapons; Xi used his opening speech to back the WTO-centred trading system.

items.title: SpaceX catches Starship's upper stage after an orbital flight
items.summary: For the first time, SpaceX caught the Starship upper stage with its launch-tower arms after a trip to orbit, a step towards fully reusable rockets. The Super Heavy booster was lost in the same flight.

items.title: COP31 in Antalya runs into overtime over fossil fuels
items.summary: The UN climate talks in Turkey were due to end on 20 November but countries remain divided. The draft cover decision calls for faster action to phase out fossil fuels and for wealthy nations to reach net zero sooner, which the EU and oil-producing countries have pushed back on from different sides.
items.why: Whatever COP31 agrees on carbon markets and finance shapes demand for Ghana's Article 6 credits: a live input for your research.

items.title: The second Global Stocktake begins
items.summary: Negotiators in Antalya launched the second five-yearly review of progress under the Paris Agreement, while finance, fossil fuels and a just transition remain unresolved.

items.title: African and island states press for faster IPCC science
items.summary: Dozens of countries, including African ones, want the IPCC's next big assessment published before COP33 in 2028, saying delays are unjustifiable.

items.title: Health service warns of El Niño risks this harmattan
items.summary: The Ghana Health Service warned of higher risks of meningitis and dehydration as El Niño is expected to affect Ghana during the harmattan season.
items.why: Plan fieldwork with the James Town processors around the heat and dust: water, breaks and shade.

items.title: MTN marks 30 years in Ghana with a $1.1bn investment pledge
items.summary: MTN is marking its 30th anniversary in Ghana and has committed $1.1 billion in new investment.
items.why: Mobile money is how Carbon Clarity plans to pay benefit shares to the women.

items.title: University of Ghana trims its hostel fee rise
items.summary: The University of Ghana cut its proposed hostel fee increase from 26% to 15%, and the government asked the tertiary education regulator to engage the Rent Commission on student hostel fees.
items.source: Daily Guide and Daily Graphic, via GhanaWeb

items.title: Nigeria moves closer to state police
items.summary: All 36 Nigerian state assemblies approved a constitutional amendment allowing states to form their own police forces; it still needs presidential assent and further laws.

items.title: AI worries drive the biggest tech sell-off in years
items.summary: Tech shares fell sharply through November as investors questioned whether spending on AI data centres will pay off; early in the month saw the largest tech sell-off since the Covid crash.

good.title: Nature restoration at record pace
good.summary: A UN Environment Programme report says about 252 million hectares of land, sea and freshwater habitat are being restored across 149 countries, the fastest pace on record.

good.title: Malaria deaths nearly halved since 2000
good.summary: The global malaria death rate has almost halved since 2000, though most remaining deaths are in Africa.

good.title: Record year for the Green Climate Fund
good.summary: The fund committed $3.3 billion to climate adaptation and mitigation projects in developing countries in its biggest year yet.

good.title: Kenya secures $160m to protect 17.3 million hectares
good.summary: Kenya secured a $160 million conservation investment to protect 17.3 million hectares of natural land.

good.title: China's emissions fall for a quarter
good.summary: China's CO₂ emissions fell 3.1% in the third quarter of 2026, the steepest quarterly drop since the 2022 lockdowns, and electric trucks reached about half of heavy-truck sales in September.

good.title: Barbados ends mother-to-child HIV transmission
good.summary: The WHO recognised Barbados for eliminating mother-to-child transmission of HIV, after testing and treating 98% of pregnant women.

future.title: Clean cooking financed by carbon credits
future.why: New government policies across Africa have helped secure about $900 million in new clean-cooking finance, with carbon credits as the main engine. The catch: it only lasts if buyers trust the credits.
future.fit: This is Carbon Clarity's core. The winners will be projects with measured, audit-ready data.
future.step: This month: map which Gold Standard metered-method requirements your pilot data already meets.

future.title: Digital MRV and high-integrity credit data
future.why: Credit buyers increasingly pay only for credits they can verify. Sensor-based monitoring and clean data trails are becoming the difference between credits that sell and credits that don't.
future.fit: Your Data Vault idea could become a service for other cookstove and agriculture projects in Ghana.
future.step: Write a one-page description of the Data Vault as a service: who pays, what it proves.

future.title: Clean heat for small industries
future.why: RMI lists clean industrial heat among Africa's six emerging climate-tech opportunities. Fish smoking is exactly this: small-scale process heat.
future.fit: Improved ovens for fish processors are a clean-heat business with income for women, not just a stove programme.
future.step: Estimate the market: how many processors in Greater Accra and coastal Ghana, and how much wood they burn.

future.title: Carbon removal from biomass: biochar
future.why: RMI also highlights carbon dioxide removal that uses Africa's biomass and soils, a market where removal credits sell for far more than avoidance credits.
future.fit: Waste biomass from smoking (husks, offcuts) could be turned into biochar: a second revenue stream.
future.step: Read one biochar removal methodology and list what you'd need to measure.

future.title: Energy-led climate tech is where African investment goes
future.why: Africa's climate-tech startups raised $6.35bn from 2016 to 2025, now the continent's biggest venture sector, with energy taking about 65% of the money.
future.fit: Pitch Carbon Clarity as energy plus livelihoods: efficient heat, solar drying or cold storage for fish.
future.step: Add one slide to your pitch: 'Why energy investors should care about fish smoking'.

future.title: Article 6 advisory for Ghanaian projects
future.why: Ghana is one of the first countries trading credits between governments under Article 6. Developers need people who understand authorisation, corresponding adjustments and the Carbon Market Office process.
future.fit: Your Ghana carbon market research makes you one of those people: it can become consulting work or a job.
future.step: Turn your Step 3 agreement table into a two-page brief you can share on LinkedIn.

quiz.q: Which city is hosting the COP31 UN climate talks?
quiz.why: COP31 is in Antalya, Turkey (Belém hosted COP30, Dubai COP28, Baku COP29).

quiz.q: Where are Trump, Xi and Putin meeting this week, alongside APEC?
quiz.why: Trump arrived in Shenzhen for APEC and a first three-way meeting with Xi and Putin.

quiz.q: Roughly how many hectares are being restored worldwide, according to UNEP's latest report?
quiz.why: UNEP reports around 252 million hectares under restoration across 149 countries.
